name: two-node-switch
description: Minimal multi-node scenario: two compute nodes share one pool through a switch with a binding bisection cap, so cross-node contention is visible in link/switch telemetry and per-node metrics. Requests shard round-robin; each node runs an independent policy instance with its own admission queue (concurrency is per node).
assumptions: Local capacity is 2 GiB per node to force pool traffic; this exercises contention, not a deployment configuration.
Switch bandwidth is set below 2x link bandwidth so the bisection cap binds; remove the switch block to model infinite bisection.
No peer routes exist in this scenario: pages move between compute nodes only through the shared pool (placement is single-owner; see ntier-spine-leaf.json for peer placement).
The workload is synthetic KV-cache decode, not a captured trace.
